![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Destructuring `password` and `name` directly from `req.body` will throw a `TypeError` if `req.body` is undefined or null (e.g., if the request has a missing or malformed body). Since the very next line uses optional chaining (`req.body?.email`), it is clear that `req.body` is expected to potentially be missing. To prevent unhandled runtime exceptions and ensure the validator fails closed gracefully, we should provide a fallback object when destructuring. Additionally, when adding robustness checks for potentially malformed or missing input data, please include regression tests to verify that the system fails closed gracefully rather than throwing unhandled TypeErrors.

```suggestion
const { password, name } = req.body || {};
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When adding robustness checks (such as optional chaining or Array.isArray) for potentially malformed or missing input data, include regression tests to verify that the system fails closed gracefully (e.g., returning a failure status) rather than throwing unhandled TypeErrors.
2. Validation functions should explicitly handle missing, null, or non-object inputs by returning a specific error code and failing closed, rather than silently returning empty failures or throwing a TypeError.
</details>
